events.text:
The Black Sea has become the world’s deadliest shipping route for merchant sailors, with more than 570 vessels struck and at least 40 seafarers killed this year.
The death toll exceeds the 24 sailors killed in the Strait of Hormuz over the same period. 
Attacks surged in the third quarter, with about 387 ships hit between July and September, more than four a day, after Ukraine launched a campaign against Russian-linked vessels and Russia stepped up strikes on ships calling at Ukrainian ports. 
Ambrey estimates Russia has been responsible for around 90% of attacks on shipping over the past 45 days, using drones, explosive-laden sea drones and missiles. 
The strikes have spread into the waters of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria, where the Comoros-flagged Khoryv capsized after a drone strike off Constanța on Friday, killing one sailor and leaving three missing. 
Greater Odesa ports handled fewer than 10 ships last month compared with about 400 in July, as shipowners describe calls at Ukrainian ports as “near suicidal” and war-risk insurance premiums soar.
Source: FT

events.text:
🇷🇺🇮🇳⚡ According to reports, Russia has offered India its most advanced air and missile defense system, the S-500, but with additional conditions attached to the proposed purchase agreement, which could complicate India’s already ambitious plans to modernize its armed forces. Russia wants a minimum order of five S-500 regiments.
India, which is seeking to eliminate critical gaps in its air defense system, is considering acquiring five more S-400 systems, almost a decade after signing the initial agreement with Moscow. Despite the long wait, Russia has still not completed deliveries under the original contract, and the fifth S-400 system remains undelivered.
Meanwhile, India’s Ministry of Defence is also considering the acquisition of one or two S-500 systems to strengthen its strategic defenses, in particular through advanced missile defense and anti-satellite weapons.
However, the new conditions put forward by the Kremlin threaten to increase pressure on India’s already overstretched defense budget.
At the same time, New Delhi is pursuing several major procurement programs, including:
⬛ 114 Rafale fighter jets, as well as Rafale-M aircraft for Indian Navy aircraft carriers.
⬛ Submarines with air‑independent propulsion (AIP) to strengthen its undersea warfare capabilities.
⬛ Large-scale replenishment of missile and ammunition stocks, after significant losses in the May conflict with Pakistan, when Pakistani strikes destroyed substantial amounts of military supplies at Indian ammunition depots, including the depot in Beas.
With several costly defense procurements competing for limited financial resources, the conditions set by Moscow for the S-500 deal may force New Delhi to make difficult procurement decisions, potentially delaying plans to build a more comprehensive, multilayered air and missile defense system.
This situation also underscores India’s continued dependence on Russian defense technologies, despite delivery delays, rising procurement costs, and competing military priorities that complicate its long-term modernization ambitions.

🇺🇸🇮🇱 Netanyahu begs Trump for help as Israeli election polls turn against him - report
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has repeatedly pressed US President Donald Trump for more public endorsements ahead of Tuesday's election, Axios reports, citing US and Israeli sources.
Netanyahu reportedly spoke with Trump twice in three days, suggested wording for additional endorsements, and even proposed that Trump speak directly to Israeli journalists.
A US source described the lobbying as a "sign of desperation."
Three major Israeli TV polls project just 50 seats for Netanyahu's coalition in the 120-seat Knesset, well short of the 61 needed for a majority. His Likud party is projected to fall from 32 seats to 20.
Trump has already endorsed Netanyahu and warned that his defeat could affect US-Israel relations.

events.text:
🇮🇳 India reveals ongoing clashes with Chinese forces along Line of Actual Control 
China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) and Indian forces have repeatedly clashed at multiple locations along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) border, particularly in Arunachal Pradesh, according to chief of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), Shatrujit Kapur.
The confrontations began in July in the Taksing sector of Upper Subansiri district and are still continuing, he said at the force’s annual felicitation ceremony.
The ITBP chief noted that:
♦️ The force’s Shaurya commandos, trained for high-altitude warfare, played a key role during the episodes. 
♦️ Measures are being taken to strengthen preparedness, including raising drone platoons in all border units, a specialized combat training module for Galwan-like situations and creation of underground infrastructure
Previously, state authorities and ministers had denied the clashes.
After the 1962 Indo-Chinese war, both nations agreed to maintain a status quo along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) - a loosely defined de facto border.
📌 the Western Sector (Ladakh) is the most contentious area, lying in the greater Kashmir region
➡️ the Middle Sector (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand) is less disputed
➡️ the Eastern Sector (Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim) includes areas China refers to as ‘South Tibet’
There have been several bouts of clashes in recent years, such as the 2020 stand-off in Galwan Valley, Ladakh.
